title: How Steve Jobs defined Apple's purpose and built Pixar's handmade home
summary: Two 2000 pieces: a private email where Jobs distills Apple's reason for being (making high technology easy for "mere mortals"), and his speech opening Pixar's headquarters. The speech shows how a building should reflect a company's soul, built with craft, collaboration and iteration like its films.

principles.text: Apple exists to make high technology easy for ordinary people to learn and use.
principles.quote: Apple is the premier company in the world at making the exploding world of high technology easy to learn and use, thereby enabling mere mortals to enrich their lives using it.

principles.text: Great products come from loving what technology can do for regular people's creative lives.
principles.quote: Because we are in love with the potential for personal computers to enhance and enrich the lives of regular people

principles.text: Marry state-of-the-art technology with ease of use so users can do more.
principles.quote: Apple marries state of the art technology with Apple’s legendary ease-of-use to create products that enable users to do more

principles.text: Demystifying technology has more impact than anything else; stores should be places to understand it.
principles.quote: Demystified technology, it will have a much greater impact than any other thing we can do.

principles.text: Designing your own space forces you to answer who you are; capture the company's soul in it.
principles.quote: But when you decide to design your own building, you have to ask the question, “Who are we?” Because you want to capture some of the soul of the company in the building and reflect who we are.

principles.text: Create through ruthless iteration: throw away early treatments, then refine endlessly.
principles.quote: First, a treatment; throw it away. Then another; throw it away. And finally, one that is worth developing—and then zillions and zillions of iterations, model after model after model, detail after detail.
